# Workshop Basics

Source: [1840](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/1840); edited 2023-04-11. Evidence: archived documentation.

Not independently verified in the current game. An article edit date is not a behavioral test date.

<a id="wiki-1840-n1"></a>

- Documented rules combine an event, all-required conditions, and actions in top-to-bottom order; contextual values depend on the triggering event instance.

<a id="wiki-1840-n2"></a>

- Event Player is the trigger's player; healing events expose Healer/Healee and death events Attacker/Victim. Local Player instead refers to the viewer and is restricted to created effects/visuals.

<a id="wiki-1840-n3"></a>

- Custom String comparisons are documented as case-sensitive.

<a id="wiki-1840-n4"></a>

- Full Copy Settings includes lobby settings plus Workshop rules/settings; native rules, conditions and actions can also be copied/pasted separately.

<a id="wiki-1840-n5"></a>

- Presets can be overwritten and are limited; updating an existing share code replaces its old contents. Article recommends keeping source text and identifying existing share code in mode metadata to prevent wrong-code updates.

<a id="wiki-1840-n6"></a>

- Archive claims share codes expire unless imported/uploaded enough and there is no in-game list of all owned codes; PC text backups are the recommended durable source, while console clipboard export is unavailable.

<a id="wiki-1840-n7"></a>

- Documented limits: players+bots 12, extendable to 24 but at most 12 real players; AI bots included, training bots excluded.

<a id="wiki-1840-n8"></a>

- Documented text limit 128 shared by HUDs, in-world texts and both progress-bar variants; no increase. Effects limit 128, extendable to 256, includes normal effects, beams, icons and Workshop-created projectiles.

<a id="wiki-1840-n9"></a>

- Workshop capability limits and runtime server load are distinct constraints; available events/actions/values bound what can be implemented.

Source limitations:

- April 2023 source; player/entity/text limits, code expiry and UI/platform details are date-sensitive and require reconciliation with newer source pages.

- Making a basic mode section is an explicit placeholder ('idk lol...'); no worked onboarding project exists here.

- Expiration description gives vague 'enough times'/'6 months' guidance, not a reliable retention contract.

- Image-only examples not fetched; all textual content read.
